messages:
alex r.: Hey folks — opened a small PR that tweaks kernel-selection heuristics and KV-cache eviction thresholds to shave tail latency and token cost. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2931  Can someone take a quick look? Mainly perf/cost changes, no API surface changes.

jin: grabbing it now. did you run the staging perf harness?

alex r.: yup, ran both local and staging. quick summary:
```
model=redwood-3b, seq=2048, concurrency=16
old: p50=21ms p99=420ms mem=3.1GB
new: p50=18ms p99=310ms mem=2.7GB
approx cost delta: -8% per 1M tokens
```

tara: wow p99 improvement looks promising. what's the stddev / run-to-run variance?

alex r.: variance ~5-7% p99 across 5 runs on staging. I can add more runs to the PR comment.

kevin: CI is failing on one of the quant unit tests though — `kv_cache_eviction_test` times out intermittently. stacktrace looks like an async scheduling hang.

alex r.: I saw that. I pushed a retry in CI and repro steps in the PR description: `pytest tests/kv_cache -k eviction -q`. It repros locally about 1/10 runs.

jin: can you drop the exact bench command and env var list into the PR so I can reproduce exactly? also add a simple deterministic unit test for the eviction path so it isn't flaky.

alex r.: added bench command: `./tools/bench --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --concurrency 16 --iters 1000` and env: `export REDWOOD_ENV=staging; export BENCH_SEED=42`. Will add the unit test — plan to expose the eviction threshold behind a feature flag so we can roll back if needed.

tara: sounds good. also make sure the kernel-selection math has comments — took me a minute to follow the heuristic. small docs in-code would help reviewers.

kevin: i'll take a full code review this afternoon — focusing on numerical stability and any hidden allocations in the new path. I can approve if CI is green and tests are deterministic.

ci-cd-bot: Preview build available: https://deploy.redwood.dev/preview/2931 (integration tests started) :white_check_mark:

jin: quick note — we should gate the rollout to canary only (dedicated customers) initially. adding @platform-team to the PR for rollout policy config.

alex r.: thanks — plan is canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on perf regressions. aiming to merge EOD if we get 2 approvals and CI is stable. :rocket:

tara: i'll validate the benchmark harness outputs and sanity-check routing fallback behaviour later today. ping me if you want me to grab extra runs. :eyes:

kevin: will re-run the flaky test locally and post results. if everything looks good i'll approve.

alex r.: huge thanks y'all — please call out any regressions in this thread. will also add a short changelog entry and notes for on-call.

jin: thanks, jumping in now.
